case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Department of Children & Families v. C.W.
key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, First District
key_cases.holding: On remand the trial court properly reweighed the section 39.810 manifest-best-interests factors, and its decision to deny termination and change the permanency goal to placement with a fit and willing relative was affirmed as supported by competent substantial evidence.
key_cases.relevance: C.W. shows that a child's bond with a relative caregiver may properly drive the permanency goal, provided the statutory factors are weighed.
key_cases.quote: Finding that the trial court's order is based on competent substantial evidence, we affirm.

key_cases.case_name: Seminole Tribe of Florida v. Department of Children & Families
key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, Fourth District
key_cases.holding: A trial court's finding of good cause to deviate from ICWA's placement preferences is reviewed for abuse of discretion, and the deviation was affirmed where the record showed the court understood the statutory scheme and found the tribal family could not presently meet the child's needs.
key_cases.relevance: It governs when a court may place an Indian child outside the statutory preference for extended family and tribal homes.
key_cases.quote: choosing to apply Florida's abuse of discretion standard to the review of a trial court's finding of good cause to deviate

key_cases.case_name: In re J.B. (J.B. v. Department of Children & Family Services)
key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, Second District
key_cases.holding: An order placing children in permanent guardianship and terminating protective supervision was reversed because the procedure used did not produce an adequate evidentiary hearing on the facts required to support permanent guardianship.
key_cases.relevance: Placing children permanently with a kin or non-parent guardian requires findings made at a real evidentiary hearing.
key_cases.quote: the procedure used did not result in an adequate evidentiary hearing to establish the factual issues necessary to support an order of permanent guardianship

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit
key_cases.holding: The caseworker was entitled to qualified immunity on the mother's substantive due process claim arising from the emergency custody of her medically fragile child with a grandmother, because no clearly established law made that conduct unconstitutional.
key_cases.relevance: The child was placed with a grandmother under emergency custody, the kinship posture at issue here.
key_cases.quote: Because we hold that there has been no violation of clearly established substantive due process law, we need not decide whether Stephens' behavior actually violated Maddox's substantive due process rights.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: ICWA section 1912(f)'s beyond-a-reasonable-doubt 'continued custody' requirement does not apply to a parent who never had custody, section 1912(d)'s remedial-efforts requirement applies only where termination would precipitate the breakup of an Indian family, and section 1915(a)'s preferences do not bar a non-Indian adoption when no preferred party has sought to adopt.
key_cases.relevance: It narrows section 1915(a), holding the placement preferences do not displace an adoption where no preferred relative or tribal family has actually come forward.
key_cases.quote: §1912(f) does not apply where the Indian parent never had custody of the Indian child.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court upheld Congress's Article I authority to enact ICWA and rejected the anticommandeering challenges on the merits, while vacating the equal protection and nondelegation rulings because no petitioner had standing to press them.
key_cases.relevance: It leaves ICWA's placement-preference scheme intact and in force, so section 1915 continues to govern kinship and tribal placement of Indian children in Florida.
key_cases.quote: the bottom line is that we reject all of petitioners' challenges to the statute, some on the merits and others for lack of standing
